newsitem.title: GERMANY: German travel agents pray last-minute boom goes on.
newsitem.headline: German travel agents pray last-minute boom goes on.

text.p: Holiday travel sales in Germany are likely to stagnate this year unless a boom in last-minute bookings continues to the end of the season, the German independent agents association ASR said on Friday.

ASR president Klaus Laepple said the German travel industry has had a "catastrophic" year but late bookings for summer holidays have now picked up dramatically because of bad weather and could generate a slight plus.
Airline ticket and rail travel sales are showing growth this year but package holiday sales are stagnating at last year's levels, he told journalists at a news conference.
Laepple declined, however, to forecast whether more tour operators or travel agencies will go out of business this year.

In the largest German travel industry collapse to date, Stuttgart-based operator Hetzel Reisen declared itself insolvent in late July, forcing alternative holidays to be found for up to 50,000 tourists.
"The travel business overall has become much more difficult since last year. Reality has reached our industry, the days of double-figure growth are past," Laepple said.
A Deutsche Lufthansa AG conference with 240 travel agents in Berlin on September 25-27 designed to debate the airline's future relationship with its agents is booked out, he said.
"The atmosphere (with Lufthansa) is not good and it goes as far as aggression. It will not be a quiet event," he forecast.
Relations have been soured in recent months by Lufthansa plans for direct Internet sales, scrapping of commission payments on airport fees and summer price discounting, observers noted.
The ASR, which represents 2,200 agencies, called on large tour operators to scrap minimal sales turnover requirements which restrict package sales through the country's 18,978 agencies.
"This would be a complete liberalisation. We would have equal competitive conditions between agents and everyone could sell what they want," he said.

The five largest operators, TUI, NUR Touristic, the LTU group, Dertour and ITS, have a 60 percent market share and effectively keep smaller operators out of agencies by their restrictive turnover conditions, Laepple said.
